speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you describe the severity and location of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urination since finishing the antibiotics?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain, burning, or urgency when you urinate, and have you noticed any blood or cloudiness in your urine? Additionally, does the pain on either side of your back worsen if I gently tap on the area just below your ribs?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any dark or cola-colored urine during the rash episode, and have you noticed any swelling in your hands, feet, or around your eyes? I would also like to request a urinalysis and serum creatinine level to check for kidney involvement. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Serum_Creatinine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Serum Creatinine: Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated eosinophils in your urine sediment is a classic sign of acute interstitial nephritis, likely triggered by your recent antibiotic use. Do you have a history of asthma, allergic rhinitis, or eczema, and did you experience any shortness of breath or wheezing during the rash episode? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative bacterial culture and specific urine findings, this is not an infection but a drug reaction. Are you currently experiencing any shortness of breath, wheezing, or new skin rashes? DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
